newsitem.title: UK: MILLENNIUM SAYS STG NOT HITTING UK HOTELS.
newsitem.headline: MILLENNIUM SAYS STG NOT HITTING UK HOTELS.

text.p: Britain's Millennium & Copthorne Hotels Plc said on Wednesday the strong pound was not affecting returns at its UK properties.
"We operate predominantly in the business market and there is no sign of the strong pound impacting our business," finance director David Cook told a telephone conference call.
Cook added that there was no indication that an expensive pound for foreign visitors was depressing "secondary" spending on items such as food and drink.

The group's average room rate rose five percent to 80.70 stg in the first six months of the year and Cook said it may be able to improve on that in the second half of the year as business customers return following the summer holiday.
"The months of September, October and November are the strongest for us as the business and conference market picks up," said Cook.
Cook said Millennium, which owns or operates 24 properties in Britain, France, Germany and New York was looking at acquisition targets.

But he poured cold water on speculation that the company was lining up a 250 million stg bid for Radisson SAS Hotels Worldwide, owned by Scandinavian Airline Systems. "I'm not sure where that story came from," he said.
Cook said Millennium would seek acquisitions across the whole of western Euorpe and the United States and added that it was a good time to be looking for hotels in France and Germany.

Millennium made a 100,000 stg loss from its combined French and German operations in the first half but Cook said this stemmed from a 1.0 million stg provision to cover the temporary closure of its central Paris hotel.

The property, acquired last December, was closed in July for a major refurbishment programme. It will reopen in late spring 1998 in time for the soccer World Cup which will be played in France in June and July.
Millennium has a total of three hotels in France plus two in Germany.
The bulk of its operating profit came from the UK, with London contributing 13.6 million stg and the provinces 7.9 million. New York made an 8.0 million profit.
